identity.name: Kingdom of Iberia (Caucasian Iberia)
alt_names: Iberian Kingdom of the Pharnavazids, Artaxiads and Chosroids

land.text: Iberia under Persian rule after the Eternal Peace of 532 ('Sasanians retained Iberia')

successors.note: Cliopatria's last Iberia shape is 533 and the sasanian-empire dossier gains Iberia in 534. The Kingdom of Iberia page runs the monarchy on to 580 ('In 580, Hormizd IV abolished the monarchy') with 'Sasanian annexation (523-580)' in its infobox; the Principality of Iberia (principality-of-iberia, c. 588) is the next state on this land.

capitals.name: Armazi / Mtskheta
capitals.note: Infobox lists 'Armazi, Mtskheta, Tbilisi' without years. 'Vespasian fortified the ancient site of Arzami near Mtskheta for the Iberian kings in AD 75.' The span is a bridge to Vakhtang I.

capitals.name: Tbilisi
capitals.note: Vakhtang I (reign 447-502) 'made Tbilisi his capital' (the page gives no year; the start of his reign is the earliest it can be). Confidence low.

correction.text: the kingdom of Pharnavaz I and his successors around Armazi and Mtskheta, the Kartli core (the Cliopatria -63 outline is the later extent)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for c. 302 to 64 BC, before Cliopatria's first shape: Pharnavaz I is 'the first king of Iberia (c. 302 - c. 237 BC)' at Armazi/Mtskheta. The page gives no extent for these centuries (it mentions Colchian and Armenian territory 'conquered from the Kingdom of Armenia in the 2nd century BC' only in passing), so the core is Kartli, approximate. The page gives no area, so no infobox comparison is possible.

-63..67: 35,868 km2. The page has Pompey draw Iberia into 'a Roman invasion in 65 BC' and lists a Roman client status 65-63 BC, with no change of land. The page gives no area, so no infobox comparison is possible.

68-259: same outline (35,797 km2). Within it: Vespasian fortifies Arzami in AD 75 and Iberia 'regained much of its former strength' under Pharsman II (116-132); no territorial event is dated. The page gives no area, so no infobox comparison is possible.

correction.text: the same outline as 68-259, a Sasanian tributary with its own king

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 260-286, which Cliopatria leaves empty: 'During the reign of Shapur I (241-272), Iberia became a tributary of the Sasanian Empire' and 'the Iberian king Amazasp III (260-265) was listed among the high dignitaries' of Shapur. The kingdom and its king persist, so the 259 outline is repeated; the sasanian-empire dossier carries the vassal tint (vassal_start 260).

287-396: 35,797 km2. 'Peace of Nisibis in 298, the Roman Empire regained control over Caucasian Iberia' (the Peace of Nisibis (299) page: 'Transfer of suzerainty of Iberia to the Roman Empire and relinquishment of the right to appoint the Iberian kings'); after Julian's death in 363 Rome ceded Iberia to Persia and the Peace of Acilisene in 387 confirmed Varaz-Bakur I as a Persian vassal. All of these are overlordship changes, not changes of land. The page gives no area, so no infobox comparison is possible.

correction.text: the 402 outline: the 397-401 dip has no page behind it

keyframe_review.note: 397-401: 35,557 km2, 240 km2 (about one cell group) below the neighbouring years. No page has a territorial event in 397-401 (the Kingdom of Iberia page has Pharsman IV only in 406-409), so the dip is treated as a Cliopatria artefact and the 402 outline is used.

402-509: 35,797 km2. Pharsman IV (406-409) 'preserved Iberian autonomy and ceased tribute payments to Persia'; Vakhtang I (447-502) 'marked a revival of the kingdom'; none changes the outline. The page gives no area, so no infobox comparison is possible.

510-522: 35,772 km2, a 25 km2 change from 509 (noise). Vakhtang I died in battle in 502 and the Persians rule again ('Direct Sasanian rule (502-523 AD)' in the infobox, whose status labels do not line up with the dates: it lists Sasanian vassalage from 27 BC, before the Sasanian Empire existed). The page gives no area, so no infobox comparison is possible.

523-533: 35,772 km2. 'The unsuccessful uprising of 523, led by the Georgians under Gurgen, weakened the kingdom'; the Iberian War ends in 532 with 'Sasanians retained Iberia' (Iberian War infobox). Cliopatria's last year is 533; the Kingdom of Iberia page dates the end of the monarchy to 580. The page gives no area, so no infobox comparison is possible.

region.text: the kingdom of Pharnavaz at Armazi and Mtskheta, the Kartli core

ledger.note: c. 302 BC: Pharnavaz I founds the Kingdom of Iberia. 'Pharnavaz, victorious in a power struggle, became the first king of Iberia (c. 302 - c. 237 BC)'; infobox 'c. 302 BC'. The page names the capital sites (Armazi, Mtskheta), not a boundary.

region.text: Iberia (Kartli), the land of Vakhtang I's uprising

ledger.note: 482: Vakhtang I rises against Persia. 'In 482, he led a general uprising against Persia, initiating a twenty-year struggle for independence.' The page does not say which ground was taken or held, so the zone is the kingdom.
502: Vakhtang I falls in battle and the uprising ends. 'he was eventually defeated and died in battle in 502.'

region.text: Iberia (Kartli), where the Persians fought the Iberian revolt and the Iberian War

ledger.note: 523: the Iberians under Gurgen rise against Persia. 'The unsuccessful uprising of 523, led by the Georgians under Gurgen, weakened the kingdom' (the Iberian War page: 'in 523, under the leadership of Gourgen, they rose in revolt against Persia' and 'received pledges by Justin I that he would defend Iberia'). The Sasanian dossier dates the same revolt 524/525 and the war 526.

532: the Eternal Peace leaves Iberia to Persia. Iberian War infobox 'Result: Sasanians retained Iberia; Byzantines retained Lazica'; 'all territories seized during the war by either side were returned' and Byzantium paid 11,000 lbs of gold.

region.text: Iberia passes to the Persians: 'Sasanian annexation (523-580 AD)' in the Kingdom of Iberia infobox

ledger.note: 533: Iberia ends as a kingdom on the map. Cliopatria's last shape is 533 and the sasanian-empire dossier gains Iberia in 534; the Iberian War page says 'Sasanians retained Iberia' (532) and the Kingdom of Iberia page abolishes the monarchy only in 580. The exact year is bridged to Cliopatria.

wars.name: Pompey's Caucasian campaign (Third Mithridatic War)
wars.outcome: Iberia is drawn into the invasion: 'drew Iberia into a Roman invasion in 65 BC' and is listed as a Roman Republic client 65-63 BC; no land changes hands on the page.

wars.name: Roman campaign in Iberia and Albania (36 BC)
wars.outcome: 'in 36 BC, Roman forces again marched into Iberia' and forced Pharnavaz II into a campaign against Albania; no territorial result.

wars.name: Sasanian conquest of the Caucasus
wars.outcome: Iberia becomes a Sasanian tributary: 'During the reign of Shapur I (241-272), Iberia became a tributary of the Sasanian Empire'.
wars.note: Years are the reign of Shapur I; the conquest itself is dated 252-253 on the Caucasian Albania page.

wars.name: Roman-Sasanian war of 296-299 (Peace of Nisibis)
wars.outcome: 'Transfer of suzerainty of Iberia to the Roman Empire and relinquishment of the right to appoint the Iberian kings'; the Tigris becomes the frontier. No Iberian land changes.
wars.note: Signed in 299 on this page ('Signed: 299 AD'); the Kingdom of Iberia page says 298.

wars.name: Peace of Acilisene (387)
wars.outcome: Confirms 'Varaz-Bakur I as a Persian vassal' in Iberia; no land changes.

wars.name: Vakhtang I's uprising against Persia
wars.outcome: 'a twenty-year struggle for independence' that ends with Vakhtang's death in 502.

wars.name: Iberian War

zones.text: Iberia (Kartli) and the forts of eastern Lazica

wars.outcome: 'Sasanians retained Iberia; Byzantines retained Lazica'; the Eternal Peace of 532 returns every territory seized in the war and Byzantium pays 11,000 lbs of gold.
wars.note: In 528 'the Persians pressed on from Iberia to capture forts in eastern Lazica' (not named on the page).

certainty.note: No survey or treaty line is given for Iberia on any page opened; the Nisibis (299) and Acilisene (387) settlements change suzerainty, not a described frontier. The Cliopatria outline (Kartli without Kakheti's east) is approximate throughout.

notes:
CLIOPATRIA ROW: seven shapes 397-401 apart, one outline (35,800 km2) for the whole of -63..533. The page has no infobox area, so no ratio check is possible. 397-401 (240 km2 less) is called an artefact. Cliopatria's Iberia and Lazica shapes do not overlap (0 shared cells) and Iberia and Albania do not overlap either.

START: the page dates the kingdom to c. 302 BC; Cliopatria starts at -63, so a new keyframe (Kartli, approximate) covers -302..-64. The 2nd-century BC extent (conquests from Armenia) is not described.

END: Cliopatria 533; the Kingdom of Iberia page runs the monarchy to 580 and the sibling principality-of-iberia dossier (eu-19-c) starts at 588. The sasanian-empire dossier gains Iberia in 534. The years 534-587 are Persian land in the map; the page's 'Sasanian annexation (523-580)' supports that, but the 580 abolition and the 581-587 interval are not drawn as a state. The Georgia row's 638-646 shape is the same outline again (136 of 137 cells shared) and is reviewed (verdict wrong, belongs to the Principality of Iberia) in the georgia dossier.

OVERLORDSHIP: Seleucid, Roman, Sasanian and Armenian suzerainty (infobox list: Roman client 65-63, 40-36, 30-27 BC, 27 BC-129 AD, 131-260 AD; Sasanian vassal 260-265 and 298-363; direct Sasanian rule 363-482 and 502-523) is vassal-tint material for the roman-empire and sasanian-empire dossiers (counterpart caucasian-iberia). The infobox status labels do not line up with the dates (Sasanian vassalage is listed from 27 BC, before the Sasanians), so they are not copied here.

NOT DATED ON THE PAGE: when Tbilisi became the capital (Vakhtang I, 447-502), Colchis and Egrisi under Iberia, the Iberian-Armenian border changes of the 2nd century BC, Peroz.
